title: Answer surface event
description: One dated, sourced, attribution tagged event affecting a search or AI answer surface. One object per line in data/events.jsonl. The JSONL file is the source of truth for the registry; every other representation derives from it.

event_id.description: Unique slug in the form YYYY-MM-DD-short-name. The date portion must equal event_date.

event_date.description: ISO date in UTC. For announced events this is the announcement date, not the date the change finished reaching users.

date_precision.description: How exact event_date is. day means the date is known to the calendar day. week means the event is known to fall within the week beginning at event_date. estimated means the date is inferred and could be wrong by more than a week.

event_type.description: What kind of event this is. sensor_spike records observed volatility only and never asserts a cause.

surface.description: The answer surfaces the event affects. Use multi only when an event genuinely lands on surfaces beyond those enumerated here.

actor.description: Vendor or origin of the event, lowercase. Known values include google, openai, anthropic, perplexity, microsoft, and observed. Use observed for events with no announcing vendor, such as sensor spikes.

title.description: One line naming the event. No trailing period.

description.description: Two to four sentences in a factual register. State what happened, what is uncertain about it, and anything a downstream event study needs to know. Do not assert causation.

source_urls.description: Primary sources for the event. Vendor blog posts, status pages, and official changelogs are preferred over secondary reporting. Required with at least one entry for every event_type except sensor_spike.

attribution.description: Confidence ladder for the event and its date. vendor_confirmed: the vendor stated both the event and the date on its own property. vendor_announced: the vendor announced the event but the rollout window or the exact date is uncertain. community_inferred: multiple independent observers converge on the event and no vendor statement exists. hypothesis: we suspect the event and say so.

sensor_corroboration.description: Third party volatility readings that coincide with the event. Corroboration is not causation and never upgrades the attribution tier on its own.

sensor.description: Opaque, stable label for the volatility panel, such as panel_a. The mapping from label to the underlying keyword set, market, and collection method is internal and is not published in this repository.

reading.description: The reading as published by the sensor, including its units or scale.

related_events.description: event_id values of related rows. A sensor_spike row points at a causal row once a cause is established. The rows are never merged.

added.description: ISO date the row entered the registry.

last_updated.description: ISO date the row last changed. Never earlier than added.
